title: AI Apps in a Flash: Ship to GPUs Without Docker — Dean Quiñanola, Runpod
talk_summary: A RunPod staff engineer demos 'Flash', a CLI that lets you run and iterate GPU functions locally (FastAPI on localhost) and deploy them to serverless GPU endpoints without writing Dockerfiles, with automatic dependency install, endpoint-to-endpoint calls, and network-volume warm caching. The talk is mostly product demo; the transferable ideas are the fast local-dev-to-deploy loop and ephemeral auto-deprovisioned endpoints.

takeaways.what_they_do: Cancelling a local dev session automatically tears down the provisioned remote endpoint, so no idle GPU instances linger between iterations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When I cancel it, it actually deprovisioned that endpoint. So, you don't have to have that lying around.

takeaways.technique: Local-first dev loop with one-command deploy
takeaways.what_they_do: Developers run the function as a local FastAPI server, test instantly, then a single 'deploy' command packages and ships it, skipping the docker build/push/execute cycle.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sometimes this one loop takes about 15 minutes depending on the changes you're doing

takeaways.what_they_do: The platform installs Python dependencies at run time inside the remote environment rather than baking a full image, so code+deps changes take effect on next execute.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what it's doing is in on the fly installing the dependencies

takeaways.what_they_do: Deployed functions call each other as if local; the platform handles addressing/routing between endpoints.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You execute a function and it looks like it's just local, but once you deploy it in different endpoints, it's all talking to each other.
